mechaber/1:main: The order of the Four Torah Portions; it contains seven clauses. When Rosh Chodesh Adar that adjoins Nissan falls on Shabbos, we read the Torah portion of Shekalim—that is, Parashas Ki Tisa through the verse about making the copper laver—and the haftarah is Vayichres Yehoyada. We take out three Torah scrolls: from the first we read that week’s regular portion; from the second, that of Rosh Chodesh; and from the third the maftir reads from Parashas Shekalim:
mechaber/2:main: On the second special Shabbos we take out two scrolls. From the first we read that week’s regular portion, and from the second we read Zachor es asher asah lecha Amalek, and the haftarah is Pakadti es asher asah Amalek:
mechaber/3:main: On the third Shabbos, which is the fifteenth of Adar, we interrupt certain study. On the fourth Shabbos, which is the twenty-second of Adar, we take out two scrolls: from the first we read that week’s regular portion, and from the second we read Parashas Parah, and the haftarah is Uzerakti aleichem mayim tehorim {Rama: See siman 137 seif 4.}
mechaber/4:main: On the fifth Shabbos, which is the twenty-ninth of Adar, we take out two scrolls: from the first we read that week’s regular portion, and from the second Hachodesh hazeh lachem, and the haftarah is from Rishon be’achad lachodesh:
mechaber/5:main: Should Rosh Chodesh Adar adjoining Nissan occur on a weekday—even on erev Shabbos—they advance the reading of Parashas Shekalim to the preceding Shabbos, and they interrupt on the second Shabbos so that Parashas Zachor falls on the Shabbos immediately before Purim. If Purim falls on erev Shabbos, they advance Parashas Zachor to the Shabbos before that:
mechaber/6:main: The days on which Rosh Chodesh Adar II may properly be fixed: the mnemonic zavadlu matches weekdays to dates, and samech–lamed for the Sabbaths on which we interrupt study: zayin–tes–vav—when Rosh Chodesh is Shabbos, we interrupt on the fifteenth of that month; the sign is zayin–tes–vav. When it is Monday, we interrupt on the sixth; sign beis–vav. When Wednesday, on the fourth; sign daled–daled. When Friday, on two dates—the second and sixteenth; sign vav beis yud vav:
mechaber/7:main: Some authorities hold that Parashas Zachor and the portion of the red heifer are obligatory from the Torah; therefore residents of villages that lack a minyan must go on those Shabbaths to a place where there is a minyan, in order to hear these readings, which are Torah obligations: {Rama: And if they cannot come, they should nevertheless be careful to read them with their proper melody and trop, as it is found written in older sources}
mishnah-berurah/1:א: (1) (a) Rabbi Adar, etc. - Abar for short is the matter of 4 Parshiyots. And it is. The Sages decreed that 4 Parshiyots should happen a year from Rabbi Ader to Rabbi Nisan in memory of 4 Deuteronomy and they are these. The first is the shekel parshah in remembrance of the half shekel matzoh that will be explained nearby that they were obligated to give to the bureau for the perpetual sacrifice each year. The second is the parashat remember to remember the deed of Amalek and recite it on the Shabbat before Purim to approve the deed that was from the seed of Amalek and to precede the remembrance of the resurrection of Amalek to its doing and as dictated and these days are remembered and done. The third is the Parsha of a red cow, and it is on the Shabbat that precedes the Parsha of the month, since it was burned in the desert near Nissan in order to delude Israel with the ashes of the sin immediately after the construction of the Mishkan, so that they would be pure and be able to make Passover at the time. The fourth parshat of the month on the Shabbat next to Rabbi Nissan in order to sanctify the month of Nissan is written in the Torah this month for you Rosh Mushas, ​​but this is not the main part of the sanctification because the main part of the sanctification is when you see the whitewash which is sanctified by the Bad and this reading is nothing but a reminder:

Yotzer — for Shacharit and also Musaf on Shekalim and HaChodesh; on Zachor and Parah they did not institute in Musaf [Peri Megadim]. If they did not read the portion of the day — no makeup to next Shabbat [Shaarei Ephraim]. If congregation forgot Shekalim — likewise other three portions — if already said weekly haftarah with its blessings and remembered, must return, take out sefer Torah, read portion with blessing before and after, then Kaddish and maftir without blessings; if remembered after beginning haftarah blessing and will complete the blessing, etc., finish blessing, say some verses of weekly haftarah [so blessing has where to apply] without final blessing, take out sefer Torah, read one aliyah of the day, after final blessing Kaddish and haftarah without before blessings, bless after blessings. If remembered immediately after final blessing on Torah — take another sefer, place by first, Kaddish, then read after maftir of day with blessings [there]. If they erred and read portions and Megillah in first Adar — must return read Megillah in second; regarding portions Beit Yosef implies no return; Darkei Moshe and Eliyah Rabbah wrote must return.

Tur HaShulchan siman 108: must be careful reading in congregation more than Megillah reading — although Megillah preferable and every mitzvah deferred before it; per most poskim Megillah read even individually; Parashat Zachor — Ashrei three who ate: positive mitzvah d'oraisa read with ten; defers Torah prohibition always serve them — therefore R' Elazar freed slave to complete ten. Tosafot Shantz: no Torah reading except Zachor; Tosafot Ketuvot Berachot chapter 2: Zachor and Parah obligatory from Torah — end. Rashal feared from this minor does not ascend maftir Zachor — although shaliach tzibbur reads Torah — what of it? we require bar chiyuva to ascend; he also reads Torah — only shaliach reads loud not to embarrass; also Parah be careful since those Tosafot imply d'oraisa; as I found in Chiddushei Mordechai — end; Moharach z"l wrote incorrectly — for minor who knows for whom they bless certainly permitted although minor reads loud — minor counts for minyan of seven; Torah reading every Shabbat d'oraisa from Moshe spoke the appointed times, etc. — Yerushalmi, brought Rif chapter HaKorei Omed — only no fixed order per reading except Zachor; Ezra fixed order for all readings; even minor not knowing for whom they bless — why not fulfill through shaliach tzibbur's Zachor reading — what difference ascending to Torah if minor — primary obligation they hear Torah reading — end his words. In my humble opinion minor not knowing for whom they bless — do not fulfill blessing through him nor reading without blessing — therefore do not call minor maftir not knowing; but knowing — appears they fulfill; siman 282 Rama ruled minor may read additional or four Adar portions — appears when knows for whom they bless.
